summary: Validation of the Kilimanjaro Safe Water Project against VCS Standard v5.0 and VMR0015 v1.0 at reasonable assurance and 5% materiality. Document review, a three-day site visit to all four zones and interviews. 1 CAR and 2 CLs were raised and closed; no FARs. The project is validated with an estimated 1,666.62 tCO2e per year.

s1_introduction.objective: To assess whether the project meets the VCS Program rules and correctly applies VMR0015.
s1_introduction.scopeAndCriteria: VCS Standard v5.0, VCS Program Guide v5.0, VMR0015 v1.0, AMS-III.AV v09.0 and the tools it cites; scope: the PD dated 30-October-2026 and its annexes.
s1_introduction.reasonablenessOfAssumptions: Reasonable assurance, 5% materiality; each assumption (X_boil, BL_fuel, n_wb, fNRB) was checked against survey data or the methodology default.
s1_introduction.summaryDescriptionOfProject: Kilimanjaro Safe Water Project: free distribution and maintenance of 3,000 gravity-fed ceramic-membrane household filters with a solar-assisted UV stage to 3,000 households (about 12,000 people) in four zones (Kibosho, Uru, Old Moshi and Mbokomu wards of Moshi Rural District, Kilimanjaro Region, Tanzania). The filters replace boiling of drinking water on three-stone woody-biomass fires. Emission reductions are quantified with VMR0015 v1.0 / AMS-III.AV v09.0.
